text: West Texas Intermediate closed at $90.90 per barrel and Brent reached $92.43. U.S. crude gained 35.63% for the week, the largest increase in futures trading records since 1983. Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remained near standstill while Gulf production reductions were reported.

meta.note: Price surge and physical supply disruption logged as single market configuration.

text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported nonfarm payrolls declined by 92,000 in February while the unemployment rate rose to 4.4%. Job losses occurred in health care, manufacturing, information services, transportation, construction, and federal government employment. Average unemployment duration increased to 25.7 weeks.

meta.note: Strike and weather referenced in report but excluded from structural classification.

text: The president publicly stated that no agreement would end the war with Iran without unconditional surrender. U.S. equity indices declined following the statement, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling more than 900 points and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each dropping about 1.6%.

meta.note: Statement and immediate market repricing occur within the same disclosure window.

text: Marvell reported adjusted earnings of $0.80 per share on $2.2B revenue, exceeding analyst estimates. Shares rose about 20% in trading. Data center revenue exceeded $6B for the year, up 46%. The company issued forward guidance above analyst expectations.

meta.note: Stock repricing and earnings disclosure occur within the same reporting event.

text: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation announced a $20 billion reinsurance program covering losses for oil tankers and maritime cargo transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The facility operates on a rolling basis and is coordinated with the Treasury Department and U.S. Central Command.

meta.note: Closely related to prior insurance measure; logged separately due to new financial facility scale and structure.
